title: Where the Evidence Ends
statement: A surviving bronze face rests on the photographed city: surfaces that can be examined, not interiors that can be possessed. Across the cut, an animal-flower manuscript offers a provisional reconstruction, then breaks into smaller guesses. The black field is taken from a photograph of space, but its silence is left intact. The boundary is the gap between a fragment and the whole we want it to prove.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

notes.note: Begin with a dark, bounded field behind a cut-out bronze witness. A narrow architectural footing will establish an orderly, observable world before the portrait is interrupted.
Open a fault through the head while keeping the lower body continuous. The missing interval will distinguish the surviving object from the mind's attempted reconstruction.
Let the patterned reconstruction break into two diminishing fragments. Their spacing leads into the unfilled black field without giving that field an illustrative answer.

notes.note: The finished canvas holds three distinct registers: the grounded photographic fragment, the displaced patterned reconstruction, and the expansive black remainder. The gaps and diminishing fragments make the boundary legible without filling the unknown. No further additions are needed.
